answer: Agents could require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn fees or influence decisions, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-voted or colluded. A single operator can still create many identities, but must fund each one separately and risks losing the deposits, so a sybil swarm becomes costly rather than free. The stake need not be a pearl from the tundra or a walnut; its value comes from enforceable loss, not rarity.
